correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the full two-parameter triangle domain. With \(p=(B+C)/2\), \(\delta=(C-B)/2\), \(\gamma=\cos p\), and \(u=\cos\delta\), one has \(0<\gamma<u<1\) and the exact ratio \(Q=(y-z)/(c-b)=2(1-\gamma)\sqrt{(1+\gamma)/(1+u)}(u+\gamma+2\gamma^2)/(u-4\gamma^3+3\gamma)\). The denominator is positive because \(u>\gamma\) and \(\gamma-(4\gamma^3-3\gamma)=4\gamma(1-\gamma^2)>0\). For fixed \(\gamma\), the logarithmic derivative has numerator \(N_\gamma(u)\) with \(N_\gamma'(u)=-2u-4\gamma^3-6\gamma^2<0\); hence any interior stationary point is the sole sign change from positive to negative and is a maximum, so the minimum lies at an endpoint. The endpoint limits are \(1\) and \(f(2\gamma)\). The derivative of \(f\) has numerator \(x^3+4x^2+x-10\), strictly increasing on \(x>0\), so its unique root \(q\in(0,2)\) gives the global minimum \(\kappa=f(q)=0.856762017555545\ldots\). Taking \(\delta\downarrow0\) with \(2\cos p=q\) proves sharpness and also shows nonattainment away from the isosceles limit. A fresh independent numerical replay over the reduced domain found no violation and converged to the same constant; it is corroborative only.
